content.title: Upheaval at VW: Group Reportedly Plans Four German Site Closures
content.lead: VW CEO Oliver Blume plans to radically restructure the group to make it future-ready. Employees are voicing criticism at ongoing company meetings. Initial decisions are expected in early September.

content.caption: The crisis at VW is escalating.
content.author: Berit Kessler / Imago

content.text: The VW board reportedly decided to close four German sites. As «Wirtschaftswoche» reported on Tuesday, Sept. 1, production in Emden and Zwickau is slated to end in 2031, at VW Commercial Vehicles in Hanover in 2032, and at the Audi plant in Neckarsulm in 2034. According to the report, the board could gradually let the plants «run empty» without needing supervisory board approval. Group CEO Oliver Blume plans to present a corresponding concept to the supervisory body on Friday. He had already failed to secure a majority for his austerity plans on the supervisory board in July.

VW Group CEO Oliver Blume announced noticeable management cuts at the threatened Emden site during a company meeting on Wednesday, Aug. 26. Given the pressure to save, the company is scrutinizing operations there and cutting a quarter of the jobs, Blume said. «All departments must contribute their part; it is a mammoth task that can only succeed together,» he added. The VW CEO emphasized the difficult competitive situation of the Emden site. Labor costs were more than twice as high as at comparable European sites, and other plants were significantly cheaper in terms of factory costs, Blume said. The plant in East Frisia is considered at risk because there is no competitive allocation for the 2030s yet.

The Volkswagen Group faces important decisions in early September regarding its planned corporate restructuring. According to information from «Handelsblatt» on Wednesday, Aug. 26, Marianne Heiss is reportedly set to return to the supervisory board and take over the vacant seat from Susanne Wiegand. This would mean the supervisory body would again be fully staffed with 20 members — 10 representatives from capital and employee sides each.

Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume emphasized the necessity of further austerity measures to the workforce. He said the company must reduce complexity, consistently streamline structures, and cut costs. The meeting at the corporate headquarters in Wolfsburg was the start of a series of assemblies at several VW sites where the board explained its position to the workforce. «Tariffs, new competitors, and geopolitical risks: the entire automotive industry is under enormous pressure,» Blume said. The VW Group had «countered early» and begun to realign the group and its brands, he added. «Our market shares are growing. But that is not enough yet,» Blume said.

zXV9bWkUqqRQ.text: Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume emphasized to employees the necessity of further cost-cutting measures. He stated that it was essential to «reduce complexity, streamline structures, and cut costs.» The meeting at the company headquarters in Wolfsburg was the first in a series of assemblies at several VW locations, where the board addressed the workforce. «Tariffs, new competitors, and geopolitical risks: the entire automotive industry is under enormous pressure,» Blume said. The VW Group had «taken early countermeasures» and begun realigning the company and its brands. «Our market share is growing. But that's not enough yet,» Blume added.

content.text: According to Volkswagen union chairwoman Daniela Cavallo, trust in CEO Oliver Blume is damaged — «not yet irreparable, but damaged nonetheless.» Cavallo said this on Tuesday, Aug. 25, in a speech to assembled employees at the automaker's main plant in Wolfsburg. The debate surrounding the restructuring had led to these tensions, she said. Cavallo told the more than 10,000 employees regarding the looming closures: «The German plants belong to the Volkswagen Group. They are an integral part.» CEO Blume was also present at the start of the multi-day company meetings. «Our trust in the board of this company, and especially in its CEO Oliver Blume, has been damaged,» she added.
The German automotive industry is in crisis. Competition from China, U.S. tariffs, and a shrinking sales market are leading to job cuts at major automakers. VW is also affected by this.

CEO Oliver Blume recently described the situation as «more than critical.» On Friday, Sept. 4, he plans to again ask the supervisory board for approval of his austerity plans. The management aims to massively cut costs and improve competitiveness.

Therefore, the workforce is concerned about jobs and the sites in Emden, Hanover, Zwickau, and Neckarsulm. To provide more clarity about the situation, employee representatives convened company meetings. 9 extraordinary meetings are scheduled between Aug. 25 and Aug. 31.

content.text: According to Blume, VW earns too little to finance its future. Previous cuts were not enough. «We are oversized. That often makes us too slow and too complicated,» the VW CEO described the problem in an interview published on the company's intranet.

Blume referred to the serious situation facing the German automotive industry. «It is not a VW crisis, but a crisis of the entire automotive sector,» he said. He cited U.S. tariffs, the collapse of the Chinese market with massive price declines, geopolitical conflicts such as in the Persian Gulf, increasingly fierce competition in Europe, and massive regulations as major challenges.

content.text: Concerns among the workforce are high. «For Emden, Hanover, Zwickau, and Neckarsulm, we cannot present a competitive allocation for the 2030s today,» Blume said recently. «Additionally, we must eliminate overcapacities of more than 500,000 vehicles per year in Europe,» he added. A decision on specific plant closures has not yet been made, according to Blume.

It is also unclear how many jobs will be lost. However, massive cuts are expected. Blume pointed out that there had been an agreement since the end of 2024 to cut around 50,000 jobs in Germany at Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, and Cariad by 2030. However, the already planned savings were not enough. «The frequently mentioned figure of around 50,000 jobs worldwide is not a fixed target,» Blume said.

content.text: Like every German stock corporation, VW also has a supervisory board. This can be roughly divided into four groups. The largest group consists of employee representatives. The spokeswomen are the chairwoman of the VW works council and the chairwoman of the IG Metall industrial union.

The other groups consist of the Lower Saxony state government, the Porsche and Piëch owner families, and Qatar as the third-largest shareholder. The supervisory board is completed by an individual who stands outside the four interest groups. This seat is currently vacant.

Blume is unlikely to push measures such as plant closures through the supervisory board for now. According to the «VW Law,» decisions on the «establishment and relocation of production facilities» require a two-thirds majority on the supervisory board.

The works council and IG Metall, as well as the Lower Saxony state government and the mayors of the VW sites, largely share a uniform position: drastic steps such as plant closures must be avoided in any case, they maintain.

content.text: In a recent online sentiment survey initiated by the works council, the VW workforce criticized the board's communication. To provide more clarity about the current situation, employee representatives convened company meetings. The board is expected to answer questions from the workforce there.

9 events are planned through the end of August, including meetings in Hanover, Braunschweig, Salzgitter, Dresden, Chemnitz, and Kassel-Baunatal. The first company meeting was scheduled for Tuesday, Aug. 25, in Wolfsburg. Emden and Zwickau followed the next day, with Hanover concluding on Aug. 31.

Meanwhile, Blume invoked solidarity among the workforce. «Everyone must pull together,» he told «Bild am Sonntag.» «We have launched the largest transformation plan in the history of the Volkswagen Group,» he said. The next few years are decisive for «who remains in the race and who drives to the top,» he added.
With agency material.
